title: Turn approved Zedu guides into a measurable content distribution programme
description: Build a distribution plan for already-approved guides, templates and research, rather than commissioning another blog or social calendar. Inventory ten reusable assets, identify relevant permitted distribution destinations, record each destination owner/rules, and define adaptations, attribution links and a review date. Deliver an asset-to-destination matrix, three example adaptations and a report template distinguishing placement, referral visits and qualified interest. Done when every proposed placement has an audience-fit reason and a permission route, with no copied private content or invented reach. Reuse existing campaign/UTM conventions. No posting, syndication, outreach or spending without approval.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Asset-to-destination distribution matrix for approved Zedu guides
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A distribution plan for already-approved guides, templates and research. Deliverables: (1) an inventory of ten reusable assets with their approval status and owner; (2) an asset-to-destination matrix mapping each asset to permitted distribution destinations (community forums, newsletters, partner sites) with destination owner, rules, and attribution requirements; (3) three example adaptations showing how one asset is rewritten for each destination; (4) a report template distinguishing placement, referral visits, and qualified interest. Every placement has an audience-fit reason and a permission route. No copied private content, no invented reach, no posting or outreach without approval. Reuses existing campaign/UTM conventions.

upvotes.reason: "Asset-to-destination distribution matrix for approved Zedu guides" has a defined audience and a clear done-state, and it addresses something the site does not currently say. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
This turns existing approved material into a permission-aware distribution plan with clear destination rules and separate placement, referral and qualified-interest measures.

Concrete, scoped deliverable that directly supports the parent goal; feasible with public evidence.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Pilot 3 assets in 3 destinations for two weeks before scaling the matrix
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The matrix lists where every asset could go. A small pilot shows which destinations actually send educators. Approach: pick the 3 strongest approved assets and 3 destinations whose rules allow posting (for example one community, one newsletter, one LinkedIn group), adapt each per the destination's rules, tag every link with UTM parameters, and run for two weeks. Done: the pilot plan, the posts, a results table (clicks, sign-ups, replies, removals) and a keep/drop decision per destination before the full matrix is rolled out.

upvotes.reason: "Pilot 3 assets in 3 destinations for two weeks before scaling the matrix" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

The matrix says where assets could go; it does not show which destinations send educators. Three assets, three destinations, two weeks, UTM tagging and a keep/drop rule is a bounded way to find out before scaling. Measurable and not covered by the accepted matrix.
Testing three assets in three destinations before scaling shows which channels send educators; tagged links and a keep/drop decision per destination make the matrix evidence-based.
A matrix of every possible destination is not evidence any of them works. A three-asset, three-destination pilot with UTM tags tests the claim before scaling.
A small pilot is the cheapest way to learn which destinations actually send educators; scaling the full matrix first would waste effort.
